rv.q: Lia Romeo gives us a tale of “what ifs” that is often touching and always haunting.
Given Still 's generosity of spirit, not to mention some up-to-the-minute political palaver and two master actors at the top of their game, it's a fine night out.
Sleekly produced and well-acted, it nevertheless leaves us with blue balls as the dramatic tumescence the actors work so hard to build deflates without reaching a satisfying climax.
The marvelous performances of her stars make one yearn for their ultimate reunion.
For all its flaws, this is a play you’ll want to talk about afterward.
Romeo has crafted a tender, insightful work that explores what was, what is, and what still might be, directed by Adrienne Campbell-Holt with a graceful delicacy even as things heat up.
